question: Do the authoritative Gate-A q2 and q3 operations compose with both typed Lorentzian Green homotopies, including cyclicity, causal support and the first q3-dependent source closure?
answer: Yes, with explicit scope. The immutable Gate-A snapshot's authoritative q2 and q3 are finite-order support-local operations on the same 386-row graph carrier as the separately content-addressed advanced and retarded Green homotopies. Their binary and ternary Green responses are typed on compact and matching past-/future-compact support classes; the q1/q2 and arity-three identities, local cyclicity and advanced/retarded adjoint relation replay with zero defects. Every finite same-orientation q2/q3 response tree is defined. For a general compact q1-closed degree-zero field, the q3 term cancels the q2 Jacobiator in the second nonlinear source, making it a cocycle and hence solvable modulo gauge by the constrained Green inverse. Mixed-sign trees, infinite-series convergence and Hadamard data remain open.

scope.theory: strict pure-Weyl ordinary-derivative generalized-auxiliary BV theory
scope.background: unit ultrastatic conformal cylinder R x S3

inputs.role: immutable authoritative strict pure-Weyl BV snapshot
independent Gate-A decision on the immutable snapshot
typed convergent advanced/retarded graph Green operator names
degree-restricted constrained and quotient field-equation inverse
authoritative common-snapshot ternary BV operation and arity-three identity
rank-386 local odd pairing and q1/q2/q3 cyclic replay

type_ledger.carrier: the 386-row suspended strict pure-Weyl graph BV bundle E_386 on M=R x S3
type_ledger.degree_convention: q1, q2 and q3 have suspended degree +1; Lambda_sigma has degree -1

spaces.PC: Gamma_pc^infinity(M,E_386), past-compact support (bounded below in cylinder time)
spaces.FC: Gamma_fc^infinity(M,E_386), future-compact support (bounded above in cylinder time)

type_ledger.q2: q2:X_S^k x X_T^l -> X_(S intersection T)^(k+l+1)
type_ledger.q3: q3:X_S^k x X_T^l x X_U^m -> X_(S intersection T intersection U)^(k+l+m+1)
type_ledger.plus: Lambda_plus:X_C^k -> X_PC^(k-1), continuously extended X_PC^k -> X_PC^(k-1)
type_ledger.minus: Lambda_minus:X_C^k -> X_FC^(k-1), continuously extended X_FC^k -> X_FC^(k-1)
type_ledger.homotopy: q1 Lambda_sigma + Lambda_sigma q1 = identity on the matching support class
type_ledger.field_inverse: K G_sigma(s)=s for s in ker N; [G_sigma K(phi)]=[phi] modulo im R
type_ledger.distribution_kernel_status: exists by continuity and the Schwartz kernel theorem; coordinate kernel bytes are not serialized

q2_locality.rule: finite-order local differential operations and the support-local canonical shear preserve support intersections

q3_locality.rule: the natural differential q3, algebraic auxiliary q3 and support-local canonical shear preserve triple support intersections

analytic_extension.import_boundary: This is a classical smooth/distributional theorem. It does not code the proof in second-order arithmetic, eliminate Choice, give a Bishop-constructive proof, or construct the Weyl metric BV propagator.

B2.support: supp B2_plus(u_1,...,u_2) subset J_plus(intersection_i supp u_i)

B3.support: supp B3_plus(u_1,...,u_3) subset J_plus(intersection_i supp u_i)

B2.support: supp B2_minus(u_1,...,u_2) subset J_minus(intersection_i supp u_i)

B3.support: supp B3_minus(u_1,...,u_3) subset J_minus(intersection_i supp u_i)

compatibility_replay.q2_response_identity: q1 B2_sigma - B2_sigma(q1 tensor 1 + 1 tensor q1) = q2, with the certified Koszul signs
compatibility_replay.q3_response_identity: q1 B3_sigma - B3_sigma q1^(3) = q3 + Lambda_sigma sum_(2,1)-unshuffles q2(q2(.,.),.), with certified Koszul signs
compatibility_replay.cyclic_chain: For a compact test leg, Lambda_plus^sharp=Lambda_minus composes with the rank-386 q2/q3 cyclic identities; every pairing integral has compact intersection support.
compatibility_replay.cyclic_noncompact_boundary: No pairing of two unrestricted PC or two unrestricted FC outputs is asserted.

polarized_finite_tree_theorem.grammar: T_sigma ::= compact leaf | Lambda_sigma q2(T_sigma,T_sigma) | Lambda_sigma q3(T_sigma,T_sigma,T_sigma)
polarized_finite_tree_theorem.retarded: Every finite plus tree is defined and lies in X_PC; its lower time bound is the maximum lower bound of its leaves.
polarized_finite_tree_theorem.advanced: Every finite minus tree is defined and lies in X_FC; its upper time bound is the minimum upper bound of its leaves.
proof: compact leaves lie in both orientation domains
finite-order q2 and q3 preserve intersections and fixed support steps
an intersection of finitely many PC supports is PC, and similarly for FC
the matching Green extension preserves PC for plus and FC for minus
structural induction proves type, support and fixed-step continuity for every finite tree
polarized_finite_tree_theorem.mixed_boundary: A plus node is not uniformly defined on an FC source and a minus node is not uniformly defined on a PC source; weighted or decaying mixed domains remain separate work.

lambda2_general_source_cocycle.input: q1-closed compactly supported suspended-degree-zero field x
lambda2_general_source_cocycle.support: S2_sigma is compact because every term contains the compact leg x, so G_sigma(S2_sigma) is defined
lambda2_general_source_cocycle.general_source_cocycle: q1 S2_sigma=0 (equivalently N S2_sigma=0 in the field-equation sector)
lambda2_general_source_cocycle.solution: r2_sigma=-G_sigma(S2_sigma) solves K r2_sigma=-S2_sigma modulo gauge
lambda2_general_source_cocycle.scope: general through the second nonlinear source for the certified q1/q2/q3 Taylor data; not an all-order or convergent Moller theorem

foundational_strength.analytic_part: classical smooth Green-hyperbolic support-space theorem and convergent spectral operator names
foundational_strength.boundary: Exact local algebra and classical causal functional analysis remain distinct evidence types.
